question: What does dietary diversity primarily emphasize in public health nutrition?

options.B: Food quality and a broad spectrum of essential nutrients
options.C: Relying heavily on a single starchy staple
options.D: Eliminating carbohydrates entirely from the diet

explanation: Dietary diversity goes beyond mere caloric sufficiency by emphasizing food quality and the provision of a broad spectrum of essential nutrients. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h1)

question: What is a common consequence of monotonous diets that rely on a single starchy staple?
explanation: Diets that rely heavily on a single starchy staple frequently lead to hidden hunger or micronutrient deficiencies due to a lack of nutritional variety. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h1)

question: What is the most commonly used reference period for measuring dietary diversity to minimize recall bias?
explanation: The 24-hour dietary recall is the most commonly used reference period because it minimizes recall bias while accurately capturing short-term dietary intake. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h2)

question: What does the Household Dietary Diversity Score (HDDS) primarily serve as a proxy measure for?
explanation: HDDS serves as a proxy measure of the socioeconomic status and economic ability of a household to access a variety of foods. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h2)

question: How many food groups are typically utilized in the FAO standard classification for women of reproductive age?
explanation: The standard FAO classification for women of reproductive age typically utilizes a 10-food group system to assess micronutrient adequacy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h3)

question: Why is it beneficial for Nigerian nurses to use FAO-standardized food groups?

options.A: It replaces the need for clinical physical examinations
options.B: It bridges local food availability with global nutritional reporting standards
options.C: It guarantees complete freedom from foodborne illnesses
options.D: It dictates the exact financial cost of local market items

explanation: Utilizing FAO groups helps bridge the gap between local food availability and global nutritional reporting standards, facilitating accurate assessments and comparisons. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h3)

question: What is the direct relationship between dietary diversity and micronutrient intake?

options.A: Higher diversity increases the likelihood of meeting essential vitamin and mineral requirements
options.B: Diversity has no impact on micronutrient status as long as calories are met
options.C: Greater variety decreases the absorption of all essential minerals
options.D: Monotonous diets provide superior micronutrient adequacy

explanation: Consuming foods from a wider range of food groups significantly increases the likelihood of meeting daily requirements for essential vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h4)

question: Which pairing represents a strategy to enhance nutrient absorption through dietary combinations?

options.B: Vitamin C-rich fruits with non-heme iron sources
options.D: Animal proteins exclusively with artificial sweeteners

explanation: Pairing vitamin C-rich fruits with non-heme iron sources found in plant foods enhances the absorption of iron in the body. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h4)

question: What is the threshold for achieving minimum dietary diversity for women (MDD-W) using the 10-food group system?

options.A: At least 2 out of 10 food groups
options.B: At least 3 out of 10 food groups
options.C: At least 5 out of 10 food groups

explanation: The MDD-W score classifies women as having achieved minimum dietary diversity if they consumed foods from at least five out of ten specific food groups. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h5)

question: What is a major advantage of using dietary diversity assessment tools in busy clinical or rural settings?

options.A: They measure exact biochemical nutrient quantities in the blood
options.B: They provide rapid, cost-effective screening correlated with micronutrient adequacy
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for patient interviews
options.D: They diagnose specific chronic diseases instantly

explanation: Despite not measuring exact quantities, their strong statistical correlation with micronutrient adequacy makes them invaluable, rapid, and cost-effective screening modalities. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h5)

question: What economic factor forces many Nigerian families to prioritize caloric quantity over nutritional quality?

options.B: Poverty and inflation limiting purchasing power
options.D: Universal free distribution of diverse foods

explanation: Poverty and economic instability limit household purchasing power, making nutrient-dense foods expensive and forcing families to prioritize caloric quantity over nutritional quality. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h6)

question: How do seasonal variations impact dietary diversity in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: They ensure a constant year-round supply of all fruits
options.B: They cause shortages of diverse produce during lean periods
options.C: They eliminate the need for food preservation
options.D: They lower the financial cost of imported foods

explanation: Geographical and seasonal variations lead to market shortages of diverse produce during dry seasons or pre-harvest lean periods, hindering dietary diversity. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h6)

question: What is a long-term individual consequence of poor dietary diversity in infants and young children?

options.B: Stunting, wasting, and impaired cognitive development
options.C: Enhanced physical height and bone density

explanation: Inadequate dietary diversity directly contributes to stunting, wasting, and underweight status, permanently impairing cognitive development and physical growth. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h7)

question: How does poor dietary diversity affect a population's vulnerability to infectious diseases?

options.B: It weakens the immune system, creating a vicious cycle of infection and malnutrition
options.C: It has no measurable impact on pathogen resistance

explanation: Poor nutrition severely weakens the immune system, increasing vulnerability to infections and creating a vicious cycle of disease and malnutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h7)

question: What is an essential component of nursing education regarding local diets and food availability?

options.A: Recommending exclusively expensive, imported food items
options.B: Translating complex concepts into practical advice using local, affordable foods
options.C: Discouraging the consumption of indigenous vegetables
options.D: Focusing solely on caloric intake without food groups

explanation: Nurses must translate complex nutritional concepts into practical advice centered on utilizing local, affordable, and culturally acceptable foods to achieve variety. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h8)

question: Which community-level activity can nurses promote to build resilience against seasonal food shortages?

options.B: Complete reliance on imported food aid
options.C: Strict fasting practices during harvest seasons

explanation: Nurses can collaborate with agricultural workers to promote homestead gardening and backyard farming, empowering families to grow their own nutrient-dense foods. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T004#GNS227_U2_T004_h8)
